chapter: Buddy Petit, Kid Thomas and working life
title: Out-of-town dances with Buddy Petit and Kid Thomas on a 60-40 split
summary: Reel 2. He worked with Kid Thomas about a year and Buddy Petit for a good while, playing Mississippi dances where the band got 40 percent.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Reel 2, Albert Burbank, January the 4th, 1962. You say you will work with many bands, huh? Yeah. Such as? Such as Buddy P.T., Kid Thomas. When did you work with Thomas? Well, that's way back, but I just can't remember. Before the break and after? Why do you remember? I don't remember if it was before or after. But I worked with him for a pretty good while, I guess for about a year or so. He did. I didn't know that. He's waiting across the room. He had a job on weekends. I played with Buddy P.T. for a good while. While our jobs was mostly out of town, he used to go to Buckaloozie and go through Mississippi, just get jobs out of those places. A lot of times in Buckaloozie, he would give the dance. He would give the dance on a 60-40 basis. I don't know what else I'd take him. He would split the band. How much would Buddy get, 60 or 40? The band would get 40. What would Buddy get? He didn't get 35 and he got five. He would get 40.
Well, who's selling tickets then? Is Buddy selling tickets himself?
He has somebody. He always has somebody that he knows or somebody out of the band.
Would he sell them before the dance started or would he just wait until the same day?
